explanation: The name of Jesus Christ, the Messiah who, according to Christian theology, is God's Son and Savior for humanity.
The act where Judas Iscariot hands Jesus over to the authorities in exchange for 30 silver coins.
The final meal Jesus shared with his disciples, during which he instituted bread and wine as symbols of his body and blood.
The garden where Jesus prayed intensely before his arrest, marked by deep sorrow and submission to God's will.
The event when Roman soldiers and temple guards seized Jesus in the garden after Judas identified him with a kiss.
The incident where Peter denies knowing his Lord three times before the rooster crows, just as Jesus had predicted.
The Jewish governing body (Sanhedrin) that interrogated and sentenced Jesus to death on charges of blasphemy.
Pontius Pilate, the Roman governor of Judea who formally sentenced Jesus to crucifixion after washing his hands of guilt.
The execution method in which Jesus was nailed to a tree (cross) and killed, central to Christian belief about atonement for sins.
